But this card, combined with the new Starting Interrupt Start Your Engines, makes podracing a nice side theme for almost any deck. Once the race is begun, both players compete, even if they don't have a podracer at the arena – though having one certainly ups your chances. Why wouldn't you start the race with the first turn? The race can be over in as little as 4 Dark Side turns with good draws, even faster if you've got a podracer at the arena. You may not have lost 6 force by then to retrieve, so you may be better off waiting a few turns. Also to make the most out of your podracing experience – and to be sure you'll win – you'll want to make sure that you have cards like [[Watto's Box]], and a handful of [[Sebulba]]'s dirty tricks like [[Pit Crews]] and [[Podracer Collision]] before you start. |combos=* [[Boonta Eve Podrace]] + [[Podrace Prep]][https://scomp.starwarsccg.org/?s=Boonta%20Eve%20Podrace Scomp: Boonta Eve Podrace]; card data [https://github.com/swccgpc/swccg-card-json/blob/d4e661ec/Light.json swccg-card-json Light.json] (commit d4e661ec). For you, though, it's a way to start annoying your opponent! This card is Jar Jar's own personal [[Bacta Tank]]. Though not as cost efficient as the Tank, since it costs 3 to pull Jar Jar back into hand instead of two, it deploys for free, isn't targeted by Shut Him Up or Shut Him Down, and has the added advantage of letting you deploy Jar Jar from reserve deck. Jar Jar can then bumble his way into your opponent's most secure strongholds, creating chaos and disaster wherever he goes. Love him or hate him, you've got to accept that Jar Jar's here to stay. And with a helper card like this, he might be showing up in the place you least want him--your deck! |pulled_by=* [[General Jar Jar]][https://scomp.starwarsccg.org/?s=Brisky%20Morning%20Munchen Scomp: Brisky Morning Munchen]; card data [https://github.com/swccgpc/swccg-card-json/blob/d4e661ec/Light.json swccg-card-json Light.json] (commit d4e661ec). '''Decipher (Reflections III foil)''' — [[End Of A Reign (Reflections III Foil)|End Of A Reign (foil)]] |sources=* [https://web.archive.org/web/20081225225012/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/index.html Star Wars CCG cardlists index] at Decipher.com (archive, 25 December 2008) * [https://web.archive.org/web/20070928014432/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/swallcards.pdf Complete Card List] (Decipher PDF, archive 28 September 2007) — Light Interrupt: End Of A Reign, Tatooine, R |strategy=By [mailto:jediknight@decipher.com Jedi Knight]https://web.archive.org/web/20040811123219/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/tatooine/light/small/endofareign.html The first Used function is okay, [[Overseeing It Personally]] was a nasty "kicker" in the old-style [[Ralltiir Operations / In The Hands Of The Empire{{!}}Ralltiir Operations]] decks. But with [[Ounee Ta]] being a more effective Raltiir Ops counter, this function alone will not justify its inclusion in most decks. The second Used function though is a great one with immense versatility. Not cheap, but to remove Dark Lord Of The Sith's choke or EPP [[Darth Vader{{!}}Vader]]'s weapon for a turn could swing a situation your way. The Lost function is also not too shabby! Emperor sees a lot of play, often in multiples so people aren't afraid to forfeit him in order to deploy another from hand. This could make them hesitate for just a second! That's a destiny 4 interrupt that works with two of the most popular Dark Side characters in the game! Definitely worth consideration in a host of Light Side decks! |cancels=* [[Overseeing It Personally]][https://scomp.starwarsccg.org/?s=End%20Of%20A%20Reign Scomp: End Of A Reign]; card data [https://github.com/swccgpc/swccg-card-json/blob/d4e661ec/Light.json swccg-card-json Light.json] (commit d4e661ec). It's not doing anything. The race is over, the concessions stands have closed, the holo-broadcasting crews have gone home, and the maintenance droids are busy clearing away the barely recognizable remains of several podracers. As is often the case with Epic Events, [[Boonta Eve Podrace]] does its thing, and then is forgotten. But the Light Side gets a second Epic Event in [[Tatooine (expansion)|Tatooine]]: [[I Did It!]] This card builds on your success with [[Boonta Eve Podrace]]. In fact, these two cards together are almost like the two sides of an Objective. [[I Did It!]] can be deployed after you won a podrace. You can place that now-useless [[Boonta Eve Podrace]] out of play to retrieve 4 force. In addition to this one-time benefit, you have several very tasty long-term bonuses. First, while you occupy a battleground site and a battleground system, you can place the bottom card of your Lost Pile onto your Force Pile. In one action, you not only retrieve a Force, but you also increase your Force activation. The second benefit is one that is likely to cause the Dark Side endless trouble. At the end of his turn, your opponent must choose to lose 2 Force or place his Force pile into his Used pile. This wreaks havoc in several ways. For one, the Dark Side will be hard pressed to save up Force to use during your turn, making it difficult to react, fire weapons that have a firing cost, and play certain Interrupts. In addition, the Dark Side player will find itself having to carefully manage his activation. If he has Force left over at the end of his turn, and he chooses to replace the cards in his Used Pile, he will have to work a little harder to track destinies. [[I Did It!]] is a powerful card that will be invaluable in building on your successes in racing.
